notes.title: Premature Evaluation: Train Valley
notes.notes:
Each week Marsh Davies boards the Steam locomotive as it chugs its way through Early Access and comes back with any stories he can find and/or is cannibalised by rabid commuters while delayed in a siding. This week he s played Train Valley, a chirpy but challenging rail construction sim.

My attempts to run a railway system make a good case for nationalisation: the absurd delays as I reverse trains back and forth over a switch in the track, somehow making the same signalling error each time; the piles of cargo that end up in the wrong town, or so late that its value has completely expired; the destruction to wildlife, farmland and neolithic monuments; the forced relocation of indigenous people. Oh, and the massive loss of life, too, I suppose. At the end of it all, I go bankrupt – and yet they keep giving me another chance.

notes.title: 36 countries and counting!

It's been a week since the game came out in Early Access, so I felt like giving you all another update on the geography of sales. And my oh my, do we have some changes:

[b][u]UK[/u][/b] has taken the lead over [b][u]US[/u][/b], exceeding it by 20%. This happened just in the last 24 hours (there must be a British review or two that just got out?).

Also, both Italy and Poland started to generate some sales, and hopefully the players from these regions enjoy their localisations, too. The same with Brazil. The only region that hasn't seen a single unit sold despite having localisation at hand is Czech Republic. Which most likely will change, once the dev team reaches some of the local media, like Level or Score.

Anyways, that's it for the sales update, and the next announcement will be from Alexey, talking about the upcoming patch/update. Happy end of the week to you all.
